instruction: Open Chrome's 'About Chrome' page to see the current browser version.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to unzip an already-extracted helloExtension directory, then navigated to chrome://extensions, enabled Developer mode, clicked Load unpacked, opened file picker to Desktop, but never completed selecting the folder. Spent 50 turns cycling between terminal and extensions page.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome to chrome:// URLs, open terminal and run shell commands, enable Developer mode on extensions page, interact with file picker dialog
metadata.failure_analysis: Model was confused by instruction to 'unzip' an already-extracted directory. After reaching the file picker in 'Load unpacked' flow, it could not complete the selection of the helloExtension folder and click Select.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests URL navigation to a different chrome:// page (About Chrome). Model demonstrated ability to navigate to chrome://extensions, so this tests the same navigation skill with a different target URL.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to chrome://settings/help (About Chrome page). Evaluator uses active_url_from_accessTree to get current URL and is_expected_url_pattern_match to verify it matches the About Chrome page pattern.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter active_url_from_accessTree correctly extracts the active tab URL from the accessibility tree and prepends 'chrome://' prefix, which properly reconstructs chrome:// URLs that Chrome strips from the address bar display.

Metric is_expected_url_pattern_match correctly receives the rules dict directly (expected.type='rule' means framework passes rules dict), accesses rules['expected'] to get the pattern list, and performs regex matching against the result URL.
Expected URL pattern 'chrome://settings/help.*' correctly matches the About Chrome page URL (chrome://settings/help).
Instruction has a single requirement (navigate to About Chrome page) which is fully covered by the URL check.
No postconfig needed since the evaluator only needs to read the current URL from the address bar, which persists after navigation.
